transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Clara Gomez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Nina Shah (Redwood CSM), Rishi Patel (CTO - Saffron), Maya Li (DevOps), Tom Hernandez (Platform), Aisha Khan (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brief):

- Network intake and SSO deep-dive scheduled.
- Redwood to provide runbook + SOC2 artifacts.

Topics covered:

Transcript body:
[00:00] Clara: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um—this is Clara from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick roll call?
[00:08] Rishi: yeah hi, rishi here, i'm the c t o, good to meet you all.
[00:12] Maya: maya from devops, thanks, we'll be implementing the peering and the config.
[00:16] Tom: tom, head of platform. we'll own the rollout.
[00:19] Aisha: aisha, security. i have a few SOC and KMS questions.
[00:22] Ethan: ethan park, i'll lead the technical bench and integration with your infra.
[00:25] Nina: nina shah, your c s m - i'll coordinate the onboarding sprints.
[00:29] Clara: awesome. quick agenda: timeline, network, sso, pilot metrics, and immediate action items. if anything else pop up, call it out.

[02:05] Clara: so we've got a proposed pilot window of may 18 to 22; that's a five-day window we use to validate latency and error budgets under a small production-like load. does that align with your timelines?
[02:18] Rishi: that sounds reasonable. we're hoping to ship a limited feature by end of june so that pilot helps. one dependency for us is the VPC peering setup and our internal firewall configs.

[03:02] Ethan: quick note on peering — we usually ask for a NAT egress rule and three inbound ports for metrics and health checks. i'll drop a network checklist after the call. we can also do a short whiteboard with your networking folks.
[03:20] Maya: perfect. i'll need the exact CIDR ranges. and when you say inbound ports, do you mean you need 443 only? our security team is strict.
[03:30] Ethan: mostly 443, but some control plane connections for the private control plane — can be tunneled over TLS. i'll include the exact port list in the checklist. sorry, sometimes the generated docs call it redwood optimiz- the — uh, redwood optimize doc, but i will make sure it's the runtime network sheet.

[05:00] Aisha: on the security side, SOC 2 type 2 is table stakes. can you send your compliance pack and, uh, any pen test reports? also where are audit logs stored and retention windows?
[05:12] Clara: yes, we have a security bundle — SOC 2, ISO summary, and pen test recap. we keep audit logs in our log store for 90 days by default, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention; i'll send the options.
[05:28] Aisha: okay, and about KMS — we need to know if keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed for the private deployment.
[05:34] Ethan: for Private we support customer KMS via HSM or cloud KMS integrations. i'll add the KMS integration notes to the security pack.

[07:10] Tom: about deployment modes — we were discussing Dedicated vs Private earlier. for this pilot we want hosted but with VPC peering and dedicated throughput, is that actually a thing?
[07:22] Clara: yeah, good question. you can start on Hosted with dedicated capacity features (reserved pools) and then move to Private if you need full control. the APIs and rollout controls are the same so switching is mostly infra and keys.
[07:36] Rishi: any noticeable latency differences? we're very p50 sensitive for interactive features.

[07:50] Ethan: latency depends on model choice and sequence lengths; we usually see an extra 8-12ms on hosted vs private in similar regions, but your workload distribution matters. for tokens-heavy calls you should look into kv cache warmup and enabling prefix caching, that reduces tail latency substantially. (laughs) sorry, that's a bit ops-y.

[09:05] Maya: can the platform do SSO provisioning? we use okta and have SCIM for user provisioning.
[09:13] Nina: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync.
[09:18] Clara: we'll need metadata from your IdP and a service account to test SCIM. propose we have an SSO deep-dive next week to capture the attributes.

[10:02] Rishi: timeline question — what's the min lead time for getting dedicated capacity reserved for our pilot?
[10:10] Clara: reserved capacity typically takes 3-5 business days to allocate once the agreement is signed, but for short pilots we can sometimes provision a burst pool in 24-48 hours. we'll surface exact timing in the runbook.

[11:30] Ethan: about benchmarks — it helps if you can give us a representative sample of payloads and a baseline qps. maya, can you send an example request shape and mean token counts?
[11:40] Maya: yep, i can pull example logs and token averages. should we anonymize PII or just scrub the content?
[11:46] Ethan: scrub PII is fine, keep structural variance so the benchmark simulates real sequences.

[13:05] Aisha: another question — data residency, we have some eu customers, do you have region controls?
[13:12] Clara: we have region-aware routing; for hosted customers you can route requests to eu-west or us-west etc. for private you can fully control region and residency. we'll include region notes in the runbook.

[14:40] Tom: runbooks — what's included? playbooks for canary, rollback, run-of-day ops?
[14:47] Nina: our onboarding runbook includes network checklist, SSO configuration steps, example playbooks for canary rollouts, rollback criteria, and a troubleshooting section with common errors and remedies.

[16:00] Rishi: success metrics — what do you normally track in the pilot?
[16:06] Clara: usually latency p50/p95, error rate under load, cost per 1k tokens (estimate), and quality regressions vs baseline prompts. we can attach an eval harness to detect regressions on your prompt set.

[17:10] Maya: evaluating quality automatically is interesting — what's the false positive rate on the evals?
[17:16] Ethan: depends on the eval design; for simple template-based checks it's low false positive, for open-ended answers there's noise. we typically recommend combining automated evals with a small human review slice during the pilot.

[19:00] Clara: okay quick recapping — agreed items: runbook, network checklist, security pack, sample payloads for benchmarking, sso deep dive. anything missing?
[19:12] Tom: rollout windows and rollback — we want detailed rollback criteria — e.g., x% error increase sustained over y minutes.

[19:25] Ethan: yeah we propose rollback if error rate > 1.5x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes or p95 latency increases by 40% sustained for 10 minutes. we can tune to your thresholds.

[21:00] Aisha: small detail — will audit logs include token-level details? we need redaction guidance for privacy regs.
[21:08] Clara: by default logs include request IDs and metadata; token-level content can be redacted or never stored for privacy-sensitive workloads. for enterprise we can enable the no-log mode or customer-managed retention.

[24:30] Maya: timeline check — when can you send the runbook and the security pack?
[24:36] Clara: i'll share the runbook and security bundle by 2026-05-10 EOD. ethan will attach the network checklist separately by 2026-05-08.

[26:00] Rishi: ok and then the sso deep dive is when? you said may 11?
[26:05] Nina: yes, proposed sso deep-dive is 2026-05-11 at 10am PT. we'll send calendar invite.

[28:00] Maya: for the benchmark, can we schedule a short 1-hour window where we run sample traffic against your dedicated pool?
[28:08] Ethan: yes, we'll reserve a bench slot during the pilot prep — likely on may 13 or 14. we'll coordinate times to match your off-peak to avoid noise.

[30:00] Rishi: competitor question — do you have customers that migrated from ModelHost? any gotchas?
[30:07] Clara: we've onboarded a few. common gotchas are network config and prompt set differences; we helped with quantization recommendations and batching settings to control cost.

[31:30] Tom: cost controls — can we set hard token caps or per-route budgets during the pilot?
[31:38] Nina: yes we have quota controls per-token and per-route, plus alerting on budget burn.

[33:00] Aisha: legal — do you have a standard DPA? we'll need that for procurement.
[33:06] Clara: yes DPA available; i'll loop in legal, but we can share the standard DPA and the enterprise compliance pack in the security bundle.

[35:00] Clara: alright, let's go around real quick for ownership of action items. rishi?
[35:06] Rishi: i'll confirm internal stakeholders and sign off on pilot window by 2026-05-09.
[35:12] Maya: i'll provide sample payloads and token stats by 2026-05-12.
[35:18] Tom: i'll review rollback criteria with platform team and come back with any edits by 2026-05-13.
[35:24] Aisha: i'll send SOC 2 questions and data residency constraints by 2026-05-09.
[35:30] Clara: and we'll (Redwood) deliver runbook and security artifacts by 2026-05-10, network checklist by 2026-05-08, and schedule the SSO deep dive for 2026-05-11.

[40:00] Ethan: one tiny technical note — if you anticipate long conversations with high seq-lens, we should enable kv-cache prewarm and maybe a quantized model variant to reduce cost during the pilot. i'll recommend settings in the benchmark report.

[44:00] Maya: what's the expected cost delta for quantized models?
[44:06] Ethan: often 15-30% cost savings with similar latency for many instruction-following workloads; again depends on model and your quality bar.

[47:30] Nina: OK file-wise, i'll create a shared onboarding Confluence space and upload the runbook + calendar invites, and we'll track action items there.

[49:00] Clara: any last questions?
[49:05] Rishi: all good for now. thanks everyone.
[49:09] Aisha: thanks.
[49:12] Tom: great, talk soon.
[49:15] Clara: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the artifacts. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription includes some auto-captions; product names may be imperfect (e.g., "Redwood Optimizer" instead of "Redwood Optimize") and some technical terms like KV cache may be split (k v cache).
